newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures settle lower, erases gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures settle lower, erases gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Wednesday on a late sell-off, erasing early gains linked to shortcovering and firming cash power prices.
"Some people thought the shortcovering rally was overdone...Bids started disappearing," said a West Coast futures trader.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 32 cents at $10.80 after posting a high of $11.10.
April COB finished down 25 cents at $10.00. Most active COB contracts ended five to 15 cents lower.
"The sharp drop in gas futures probably contributed to the fall in PV (Palo Verde)," he added.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 55 cents at $13.10 after hitting a session high of $13.65.
April PV finished down 10 cents at $12.20 after traded in a 15 cent range. Other active PV ended 20 to 55 cents lower.
NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures finished down 6.7 cents at $2.430 per million British thermal units after falling as low as $2.400.
Firm, peak electricity prices for Thursday at COB jumped $1.50 from Tuesday, while those at PV climbed 50-75 cents.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average two to four degrees Fahrenheit above normal in northern areas and three to six degrees above normal in southern areas late this week, although temperatures were called to drop to near normal over the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to stay two to four degrees below normal through the same period due to clouds and light precipitation.
Brokers and traders said they expect the power contracts would test lower levels Thursday on re-emerging bearish sentiments due to ample hydroelectric supplies and tepid heating demand in the West.
Separately, the 790 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power station near Laughlin, Nev., restarted today after being shut last Friday to repair a tube leak.
A 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut last Saturday for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for up to two weeks.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., boosted its output to 68 percent capacity from Tuesday's 59 percent following work on its recirculation pumps.
